subject: gk
question: After which infamous incident of 1919 was the Hunter Commission appointed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jallianwala Bagh massacre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Jallianwala Bagh massacre** occurred on **April 13, 1919**, in **Amritsar, Punjab**, where British troops under the command of Brigadier General **Reginald Dyer** opened fire on a peaceful gathering.
 
• The gathering was protesting against the **Rowlatt Act**, which allowed the British colonial government to imprison Indians without trial, severely restricting civil liberties.
 
• At least **379 people were killed**, though the exact number is disputed, with estimates ranging from several hundred to over a thousand.
 
• The massacre led to widespread outrage across India and played a significant role in galvanizing the Indian independence movement.
 
• As a result, the British government appointed the **Hunter Commission** in 1919 to investigate the massacre. However, the Commission was criticized for its whitewashing of Dyer's actions and its failure to hold him accountable.
 
• The massacre became a symbol of British oppression and fueled the demand for **self-rule** (Swaraj) in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kheda mill strike**__

 __
 
• The **Kheda mill strike** took place in 1918 in Gujarat. It was led by **Gandhi** and other leaders as part of the broader **Non-Cooperation Movement**, with workers protesting against wage cuts and high rents.
 
• Unlike the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the strike was non-violent, and its success contributed to Gandhi's growing prominence in India's struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Komagata Maru incident**__
 
 
• The **Komagata Maru incident** occurred in 1914 when a ship carrying 376 passengers, mostly from **Punjab**, was turned back from Canada due to the country's discriminatory immigration policies.
 
• The incident highlighted the harsh conditions faced by Indians under colonial rule but was not directly linked to the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
